perOption.C: While higher memory can slightly reduce cold start time (larger packages initialize faster at higher CPU), this is not the primary reason for faster execution.
perOption.D: Network bandwidth is separate from memory allocation. Not a direct relationship.

question: A company wants to use AWS Organizations to prevent any member account from launching EC2 instances outside of us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Which mechanism enforces this?

options.text: IAM policy on every user in every account denying EC2 actions in other Regions
AWS Config rule to detect instances launched in wrong Regions
SCP denying ec2:RunInstances with a condition on the requested Region
AWS Budgets alarm if instances are detected in other Regions

explanation.correct: An SCP with a Deny effect and Condition: StringNotLike aws:RequestedRegion for the allowed regions prevents EC2 instance launches in any other region across all accounts in the OU.

perOption.A: IAM policies on individual users require maintaining policies in every account for every user. Hard to maintain and can be bypassed by account admins who can modify IAM policies.
perOption.B: Config rules detect violations after the fact. Doesn't prevent the instance from being launched.
perOption.C: CORRECT. SCP example: Deny ec2:RunInstances where aws:RequestedRegion is not in [us-east-1, eu-west-1]. Applied to the Organization root → applies to all accounts, all users, including account admins. Preventive control.
perOption.D: Budget alarms notify after spending occurs. Doesn't prevent the action.

question: A company has significant cross-AZ data transfer costs. They use a Network Load Balancer that distributes traffic across EC2 instances in three AZs. What change reduces cross-AZ data transfer costs?

options.text: Switch from NLB to ALB (ALB has free cross-zone load balancing)
Disable NLB cross-zone load balancing
Move all instances to one AZ
Enable NLB cross-zone load balancing

explanation.correct: NLB charges $0.01/GB for cross-AZ traffic when cross-zone load balancing is enabled. Disabling it means each NLB node only routes to targets in its own AZ, eliminating cross-AZ transfer charges. Ensure enough instances per AZ for proper load distribution.

perOption.A: ALB cross-zone load balancing IS free — but switching load balancers is a bigger change. The question asks about reducing NLB cross-AZ costs specifically.
perOption.B: CORRECT. NLB cross-zone off: traffic from NLB node in AZ-A goes only to targets in AZ-A. No cross-AZ charges. Trade-off: AZ must have enough capacity independently.
perOption.C: Single AZ eliminates cross-AZ charges but creates availability risk. Not recommended for production.
perOption.D: Enabling cross-zone load balancing would INCREASE NLB cross-AZ charges.

question: A company runs a DynamoDB table with provisioned throughput. The table receives consistent 1,000 RCU/WCU during business hours but near-zero traffic at night. They want to optimize costs while maintaining performance. Which is the MOST cost-effective solution?

options.text: Keep provisioned capacity at 1,000 RCU/WCU 24/7
Switch to DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode
Use DynamoDB auto-scaling with min of 5 RCU/WCU and max of 1,000 RCU/WCU
Create a separate table for business hours and off-hours traffic

explanation.correct: DynamoDB auto-scaling adjusts provisioned capacity based on actual utilization. During business hours, it scales to 1,000 RCU/WCU. At night, it scales down to the minimum (5 RCU/WCU). Provisioned capacity is much cheaper per unit than on-demand at high volumes.

perOption.A: Provisioned at 1,000 24/7 pays for night capacity that's unused. Wasteful.
perOption.B: On-demand pricing: more expensive per RCU/WCU than provisioned (approximately 6x more per unit). At 1,000 RCU/WCU during business hours, on-demand would cost significantly more than provisioned with auto-scaling.
perOption.C: CORRECT. Auto-scaling: scales down to 5 RCU/WCU at night (near-zero cost), scales up to 1,000 during business hours. Provisioned pricing at 1,000 RCU/WCU is cheaper than on-demand. Best of both worlds.
perOption.D: Separate tables is complex and doesn't change the fundamental cost structure.
